title: Ireland Stun T20 World Champions India With Historic 2-0 Series Sweep in Belfast
excerpt: Jai Moondra's devastating spell and Harry Tector's half-century hand India their first T20 bilateral series loss since 2023 as Ireland's cricket revolution gathers pace.
body:
• Ireland beat India by one run in the second T20I in Belfast to complete a historic 2-0 series sweep — their first-ever victories over India in any format
  • Player-of-the-series Jai Moondra took 3-32, dismissing both Indian openers in the first over of the chase
  • Harry Tector scored 53 for Ireland, while Tilak Varma's fighting 55 was not enough for India
  • This is India's first T20 bilateral series defeat since January 2024, and Shreyas Iyer's first loss as T20I captain

A Stunning Upset in Belfast

Ireland rewrote the record books on a rain-disrupted afternoon in Belfast, beating the reigning T20 World Cup champions by one run to seal a 2-0 series whitewash — the first time Ireland have ever beaten India in men's international cricket.

After earning a breakthrough victory in the first match on Friday, Ireland doubled down. Put in to bat, the hosts recovered from a shaky start — both openers falling inside three overs — through Harry Tector's composed 53 and Ben Calitz's aggressive 37 to post 154-8.

India's chase fell apart immediately. Jai Moondra, the player of the series, struck with the very first ball, dismissing opener Sanju Samson. Abhishek Sharma followed in the same over, and when Moondra bowled captain Shreyas Iyer in the third over, India were reeling at 19-3.

"I challenged the lads the other day to show the world that the first win wasn't a one-off. We have a lot of lads with very few caps but they showed great character."

— Lorcan Tucker, Ireland captain

Varma Fights Alone

Tilak Varma's 55 off 46 balls kept India in the hunt, mixing caution with calculated aggression. But Matt Hollard's three-wicket haul chipped away at the middle order, and when wicketkeeper Tucker pouched Varma off Hollard's bowling, the visitors' hopes dimmed.

Harshit Rana mounted a late charge — 21 off just 10 balls — and India needed eight runs from the final two deliveries. But Rana was caught attempting a six off Harry Tector's penultimate delivery, sealing Ireland's win and sending the Belfast crowd into raptures.

A Wake-Up Call for India

The defeat is India's first T20 bilateral series loss since January 2024 and raises uncomfortable questions about the team's preparation and selection under new captain Shreyas Iyer. India rested several senior players for the tour, but the performance of the second-string side was well below expectations.

"Kudos to Ireland, the way they played. Showed professionalism, they had tremendous idea of how the wicket was going to play," Iyer acknowledged after the match.

For Ireland, the result is transformative. Cricket Ireland Chair Brian MacNeice called it a "very significant milestone" and pointed to the European T20 Premier League as a platform to sustain this momentum. "Our ambition is to continue to be competitive at the highest level," he said.

India now head to England for a five-match T20 series and three ODIs, where the spotlight on team composition and batting depth will be intense.
